subject: math
title: Grade 2 Equality and Missing Numbers
seo_title: Grade 2 Equality and Missing Numbers Worksheets: Free Math with Answer Key (Ontario Curriculum)
standard_text: Determine what needs to be added to or subtracted from addition and subtraction expressions to make them equivalent
meta_desc: Free Grade 2 math worksheets on equality for the Ontario curriculum: balances and the equal sign, true or false equations, missing numbers like □ + 7 = 15, making both sides equal and word problems. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: The equal sign means “is the same as”. Both sides of an equation must be the same.
body_html:
The = sign means “the same as”

An equation has an = sign. The = sign means both sides are the same. Think of a balance. When both sides are the same, it is level.

An equation is true when both sides are the same. 9 + 4 = 10 + 3 is true. 9 + 4 = 13 + 3 is false, because 13 + 3 is 16.

Find the missing number

A box □ stands for a number we do not know. A symbol like ★ works the same way. Count on, or use subtraction. Then put your number in the box to check.

EquationDo thisBox
□ + 7 = 1515 − 78
30 = 18 + □count on from 18 to 3012
13 − □ = 513 − 58
□ − 6 = 99 + 615
Example

□ − 6 = 9

The box is the number you start with. Undo − 6 by adding: 9 + 6 = 15. Check: 15 − 6 = 9.

Answer: 15

Make both sides equal

Work out the side you know first. Then find what the other side needs.

Example

20 + 5 = 15 + □

The left side is 20 + 5 = 25. So 15 + □ = 25. 25 − 15 = 10.

Answer: 10

Example

What must be added to 20 + 4 to make 30?

20 + 4 = 24. Count on from 24 to 30: 6.

Answer: 6

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
20 + 5 = 15 + □, so □ = 2525 is the left side. 15 + □ = 25, so □ = 10
7 + 3 = □ + 4, so □ = 10The = sign is not “the answer is”. □ + 4 = 10, so □ = 6
□ + 7 = 15, so □ = 22 (15 + 7)Subtract: 15 − 7 = 8
□ − 6 = 9, so □ = 3 (9 − 6)Undo − 6 by adding: 9 + 6 = 15
30 − 18 = 28 (smaller digit from larger)Count on: 18 to 20 is 2, 20 to 30 is 10. 30 − 18 = 12

faq.q: What does the equal sign mean in Grade 2 math?
faq.a: The equal sign means “is the same as”, not “the answer is”. In 20 + 5 = 15 + □, both sides must be 25, so the box is 10, not 25.

faq.q: How do you find the missing number in □ + 7 = 15?
faq.a: Count on from 7 to 15, or subtract: 15 − 7 = 8. Then check by putting 8 in the box: 8 + 7 = 15.

faq.q: What is equality in the Grade 2 Ontario math curriculum?
faq.a: In the Algebra strand (C2.1 to C2.3), Grade 2 students use symbols for unknown numbers, find what to add or take away to make two expressions equal, and show equal relationships with numbers up to 100.

faq.q: How can I help my child with true or false equations at home?
faq.a: Write an equation like 9 + 4 = 10 + 3 and ask your child to work out each side. If both sides are the same number, it is true. A kitchen scale or a toy balance shows the idea well.

What number goes in the box?
items.e: Think: what adds to 7 to make 15? Count on from 7 to 15, or subtract: 15 − 7 = 8. Check: 8 + 7 = 15. Not 22: that adds. Not 12: regroup a ten, do not take the smaller digit from the larger.

What number goes in the box?

items.q: In 9 + □ = 15, what does the box stand for?
c: a number we do not know
items.e: The box stands for a number we do not know yet. Here it is 6, because 9 + 6 = 15. The answer to 9 + □ is 15, but the box itself is not 15.

items.q:
What number must be added to 20 + 4 to make both sides equal?
20 + 4 + □ = 30
items.e: 20 + 4 = 24. Count on from 24 to 30: 6. So add 6. Not 24: that is 20 + 4. Not 10: that forgets the 4.

items.q:
What number must be added to 15 + 10 to make both sides equal?
15 + 10 + □ = 20 + 20
items.e: The right side is 20 + 20 = 40. The left side has 15 + 10 = 25. 40 − 25 = 15. So add 15. Not 40: that is the right side. Not 5: that only compares 15 and 20.

items.q:
What number must be taken away from 30 + 15 to make both sides equal?
30 + 15 − □ = 40
items.e: 30 + 15 = 45. To get from 45 down to 40, take away 5. Not 45: that is the left side. Not 10: that only compares 30 and 40.

items.q:
What number must be taken away from 50 − 10 to make both sides equal?
50 − 10 − □ = 30
items.e: 50 − 10 = 40. To get from 40 down to 30, take away 10. Not 40: that is 50 − 10. Not 20: that is 50 − 30 and forgets the − 10.

items.q: Ava has 8 hockey cards. She gets some more. Now she has 15. Which equation matches?
items.e: Ava starts with 8, gets some more and ends with 15: 8 + □ = 15. The box is 7.

items.q: Ava has 8 hockey cards. She gets some more. Now she has 15. How many cards did she get?
items.e: 8 + □ = 15. Count on from 8 to 15, or 15 − 8 = 7. Not 23: that adds.

items.q: Amira picks 27 apples at the orchard. She wants 40 apples. How many more does she need to pick?
items.e: 27 + □ = 40. Count on: 27 to 30 is 3, 30 to 40 is 10. 3 + 10 = 13. Not 67: that adds. Not 23: when you regroup, 4 tens becomes 3 tens.

items.q: There are 30 Canada geese on a pond. Some fly away. Now 12 are left. How many flew away?
items.e: 30 − □ = 12. 30 − 12 = 18. Check: 30 − 18 = 12. Not 42: that adds. Not 22: that takes the smaller digit from the larger.

items.q: There are some loons on a lake. 7 more loons land. Now there are 19. Which equation matches?
items.e: Some loons (the box), plus 7 more, make 19: □ + 7 = 19. The box is 12.

items.q: There are some loons on a lake. 7 more loons land. Now there are 19. How many loons were there at first?

items.e: □ − 9 = 16. Undo − 9 by adding: 16 + 9 = 25. Check: 25 − 9 = 16. Not 7: that subtracts. Not 15: that forgets the regrouped ten.

items.q: Noah has 50¢. He buys a freezie for 35¢. How much money does he have left?
items.e: 35 + □ = 50. Count on from 35¢ to 50¢: 5¢ to 40¢, then 10¢ to 50¢. 5¢ + 10¢ = 15¢. Not 85¢: that adds. Not 25¢: that takes the smaller digit from the larger.

items.q: A Grade 2 class runs laps for the Terry Fox Run. The goal is 60 laps. They run 35 laps. How many more laps do they need?
items.e: 35 + □ = 60. Count on: 35 to 40 is 5, 40 to 60 is 20. 5 + 20 = 25. Not 95: that adds. Not 35: that takes the smaller digit from the larger.

items.q: A sugar shack has 45 bottles of maple syrup. It sells some. Now 20 are left. How many did it sell?
items.e: 45 − □ = 20. 45 − 20 = 25. Check: 45 − 25 = 20. Not 65: that adds. Not 20: 20 is what is left.

items.q: Chloe has 20 red blocks and 5 blue blocks. Owen has 15 blocks. Owen wants the same number as Chloe. Which equation shows how many more blocks Owen needs?
items.e: The two totals must be the same: 20 + 5 = 15 + □. 20 + 5 = 25, so the box is 10.

items.q: Maya has 10 stickers and gets 6 more. Zoe has 12 stickers. How many more does Zoe need to have the same number as Maya?
items.e: 10 + 6 = 12 + □. 10 + 6 = 16. So 12 + □ = 16, and the box is 4. Not 16: that is Maya’s total. Not 8: 12 is more than 10, so Zoe needs fewer than 6.

items.q: The school library has 70 books on a shelf. 38 are in English. The rest are in French. How many are in French?
items.e: 38 + □ = 70. 70 − 38 = 32. Count on: 38 to 40 is 2, 40 to 70 is 30. Not 108: that adds. Not 48: that takes the smaller digit from the larger.

items.q: Lucas’s family needs 36 buns for Thanksgiving dinner. They have 18. How many more do they need?
items.e: 18 + □ = 36. 36 − 18 = 18. Check: 18 + 18 = 36. Not 54: that adds. Not 22: that takes the smaller digit from the larger.

items.q: Mateo’s family drives 90 km to the cottage. They stop for lunch after 55 km. How far do they still have to drive?
items.e: 55 + □ = 90. Count on: 55 to 60 is 5, 60 to 90 is 30. 5 + 30 = 35 km. Not 145: that adds. Not 45: that takes the smaller digit from the larger.

items.q: Kai works out 52 − 18 = 34. Which equation can he use to check his answer?
items.e: Check a subtraction with addition. Add the answer and the number taken away: 34 + 18 = 52. It is true, so 34 is right.

items.q: The school wants to collect 100 cans for the food bank. It has 65 cans. How many more cans does it need?
items.e: 65 + □ = 100. Count on: 65 to 70 is 5, 70 to 100 is 30. 5 + 30 = 35. Not 165: that adds. Not 45: that counts 4 tens instead of 3.

items.q: A Grade 2 class has 23 students. On a snow day, only 15 come to school. How many stay home?
items.e: 15 + □ = 23. Count on: 15 to 20 is 5, 20 to 23 is 3. 5 + 3 = 8. Not 38: that adds. Not 12: that takes the smaller digit from the larger.

items.q: Arjun has 30 red beads and 25 blue beads. Hana has 40 beads. How many more beads does Hana need to have the same number as Arjun?
items.e: 30 + 25 = 40 + □. 30 + 25 = 55. So 40 + □ = 55, and the box is 15. Not 55: that is Arjun’s total. Not 35: 40 is more than 30, so Hana needs fewer than 25.
